dedupe_keys.name: railsim hybrid micro and mesoscopic railway operation simulation in matsim

description: railsim is an open-source module that extends the agent-based transport simulation framework MATSim to simulate trains and their interactions with railway infrastructure, described by Ihab Kaddoura, Merlin Unterfinger, Thomas Hettinger, Christian Rakow and colleagues at the 15th International Conference on Ambient Systems, Networks and Technologies (ANT 2024, Procedia Computer Science). Coverage: microscopic, mesoscopic or hybrid micro-mesoscopic set-ups fully integrated in MATSim; trains have a spatial length across several infrastructure segments and accelerate and decelerate by vehicle and infrastructure attributes and the capacity ahead; trains reserve infrastructure elements (fixed block segments and moving blocks) and reservation requests interact. An illustrative Switzerland case shows that a capacity of 3 trains per section and 10 per station lets most trains reach their destinations, while lower capacities cause disruptions. Format and access: a conference article; the TRID record carries the abstract. Licence and cost: the module is described as open source; the licence is not stated in the abstract. Caveats: an illustrative case, not a calibrated national model. The module can run rail capacity planning and disruption scenarios inside multimodal agent-based simulations. It relates to MATSim and the ProRail OpenTrack timetable simulation in the catalogue.
